I went to the grocery store after work last Thursday.
It was a normal trip, and I only needed a few things.
I grabbed a small basket and walked toward the vegetables.
While I picked out some tomatoes, I heard someone say my name.
I turned around, a little confused, since I didn't recognize the voice at first.
Then I saw her face clearly, and everything changed.
It was Mei, a friend from elementary school, standing right there.
I hadn't seen her in almost fifteen years, maybe longer.
We used to sit next to each other in class every single day.
We both stood there for a second, just staring at each other.
Then we both smiled at the same time, almost like a mirror.
She looked older, but I could still see her old smile clearly.
We started talking right away, right there between the vegetables.
We asked each other simple questions first, like where we lived now.
It turned out she lived only a few streets away from me.
I couldn't believe we had never crossed paths before, especially living so close together.
We talked about our old classmates and what happened to some of them.
A few names brought back memories I had almost completely forgotten.
Another shopper had to walk around us because we were blocking the aisle.
We laughed and moved our baskets closer to the shelf.
Neither of us wanted to stop talking just yet.
We decided to get coffee together after we finished shopping quickly.
We sat in a small cafe next to the store for almost two hours.
It felt like no time had passed at all since school.
She told me about her job, her family, and her new apartment nearby.
I told her about my life too, and we found many things we still had in common.
It was strange how easy it felt to talk again, like fifteen years had barely mattered at all.
Before we left, we exchanged numbers properly this time, not like the old days.
We promised not to lose touch again after all these years apart.
I walked home that evening, smiling the whole way.
Now, we meet for coffee almost every single month, usually on a Sunday.
One trip to buy tomatoes brought back a friendship I thought I had lost.
Sometimes the store has more waiting for you than just groceries, and this time it gave me back an old friend.
